title: MLINE-referenced simple LTYPE with two ordered XDATA entity references

scope.source: Runtime-generated DXF; no repository drawing fixture is used or added.
scope.cross_product: Both source encodings were exported to both output encodings.
scope.linetype: EditDash, two simple dash segments [1.0, -0.5], declared length 1.5, source flags 0, alignment 65.

documents.title: DXF Group Codes in Numerical Order Reference
documents.relevant_rule: Group 1005 is an entity handle in extended data, encoded as a hexadecimal string of up to 16 digits.

documents.title: Persistent Inter-Object Reference Handles (DXF)
documents.relevant_rule: XDATA group 1005 handles behave as soft pointers and translate when referenced objects are copied or inserted.

implementation.change: The selected MLINE simple-LTYPE path accepts up to two ordered XDATA group-1005 references. It binds each typed value to a distinct ordered physical reference, a uniquely captured live LINE, and its source owner; accounts for retained entity/owner state; validates each source value during output projection; and rewrites both handles through the entity remap table. A third group-1005 reference remains refused.
implementation.preserved_contract: No public API or DRW_Interface virtual changes. Other target record types/sections and versions remain outside this selected path.

proof.source: Exact ordered raw and typed XDATA agrees. Both source handles bind in order to distinct captured LINE identities in ENTITIES with a model-space BLOCK_RECORD owner.
proof.output: Across the AC1027 ASCII/binary input/output cross-product, physical output contains the exact ordered XDATA values with two remapped, distinct LINE handles. Fresh import verifies both typed references, both emitted LINE identities, and their model-space ownership.
proof.failure_retry: Removing the second target LINE refuses and preserves the destination; restoring it succeeds on the same adapter. A late mutation of the second target's handle also refuses atomically; restoring it succeeds on the same adapter. A runtime source with three ordered 1005 references imports but export refuses and preserves the destination, enforcing the selected two-reference boundary.

limits: Only two ordered group-1005 pointers are admitted in one AC1027 simple-LTYPE XDATA profile under one bare APPID; the tested targets are two distinct model-space LINE entities in ENTITIES. A third pointer is refused. Other target types, sections, owners, versions, APPID counts/metadata, XDATA compositions and broader LTYPE schemas remain unqualified.

The evidence proves bounded transport, ownership and identity remapping only. It does not establish application-specific XDATA meaning, MLINE rendering, recursive document closure or general format support.
next: Select the next current P2 witness from the remaining named-resource body profiles. Prefer the existing three-APPID-group boundary (current provider admission caps at two); bind the exact APPID identities and output order before changing its cap. Keep other semantic/platform gates independent.
